protocol_and_eligibility.research_question: What does this review assess: the effects of clinically indicated removal versus routine removal of PVCs?
protocol_and_eligibility.eligibility_inclusion_criteria: Types of studies We included all randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing routine removal of PVC with removal when clinically indicated. We excluded cross-over trials to maintain consistency and avoid potential confounding from carryover effects. Although such designs may increase power or reduce contamination, and are permitted in the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions [40], their inclusion would have introduced heterogeneity in design and analysis. Types of participants We included any patient requiring a PVC to be in situ for at least three days for the administration of intermittent or continuous therapy (this may include patients in hospitals, nursing homes orin community settings). We excluded patients receiving parenteral nutrition. Types of interventions We included short PVCs made of any material and covered by any dressing (for example, gauze or polyurethane). We included clinically indicated removal versus any time duration for routine removal (e.g. 48 or 72 hours). We excluded steel catheters, midline catheters and long peripheral catheters. Outcome measures The critical and important outcomes in this review include PVC endpoints considered adverse events for PVCs. Critical outcomes •Catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI, defined as a positive blood culture from a peripheral vein; clinical signs of infection; no other apparent source for the bloodstream infection except the intravenous (IV) catheter; and colonised IV catheter tip culture with the same organism as identified in the blood) •Primary bloodstream infection (defined as a laboratory- confirmed bloodstream infection drawn from a peripheral vein while an IV catheter is in situ or for 48 hours after removal, with no other identified source of the infection) •Local...
protocol_and_eligibility.eligibility_exclusion_criteria: We excluded cross-over trials to maintain consistency and avoid potential confounding from carryover effects. We excluded patients receiving parenteral nutrition. We excluded steel catheters, midline catheters and long peripheral catheters.
